- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if price has recently dipped.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days) — apply downward bias to initial forecast points.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or align with sentiment decay.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model fails to adjust — force mean reversion toward recent 7–14 day average if sentiment turns negative.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.33) — increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate for lack of bullish momentum.
- For 30-day forecasts, avoid extreme outliers (e.g., >15% above or below 14-day moving average) unless sentiment strongly supports them.
